gloss: to look old and worn; to become shabby with age

definitions.gloss: to look old and worn; to become shabby with age
definitions.explanation: For objects or buildings to show visible signs of age and deterioration.

examples.japanese: {古|ふる}ぼけた{本|ほん}が{並|なら}んでいる。
examples.english: Old, worn books are lined up.

examples.japanese: この{建物|たてもの}はすっかり{古|ふる}ぼけてしまった。
examples.english: This building has become completely run-down.

examples.japanese: {古|ふる}ぼけた{写真|しゃしん}の{中|なか}に、{若|わか}い{頃|ころ}の{祖母|そぼ}の{姿|すがた}が{写|うつ}っていた。
examples.english: In the faded old photograph, my grandmother's figure from her younger days was captured.

notes:
A descriptive verb that conveys the appearance of age and wear on physical objects. Composed of {古|ふる}い (old) and ぼける (to become blurred/faded). Most often appears in the past participle form {古|ふる}ぼけた as a modifier before nouns. It can carry a nostalgic or atmospheric tone, or simply describe decay.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {古|ふる}ぼけた{家|いえ}: a run-down house
- {古|ふる}ぼけた{写真|しゃしん}: a faded old photograph
- {古|ふる}ぼけた{本|ほん}: a worn old book
- {古|ふる}ぼけた{看板|かんばん}: a weathered old sign

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {古|ふる}びる: to grow old; to show age — similar meaning but slightly more neutral, less emphasis on shabbiness
- {老朽化|ろうきゅうか}する: to deteriorate with age — a formal term used for infrastructure, buildings, and equipment
- くたびれる: to be worn out — focuses on being tired or used up, applies to clothes and people

forms.label: ている past polite
forms.negative: {古|ふる}ぼけていませんでした
